observation_or_problem: Proposal (submitted 9 Sep) ranks events into deciles within each quarter and lets Rule B trade at the close that generates its signal; both use information not available at decision time.
action_or_experiment: Re-read methodology against the brief's leakage criteria.
result: Within-quarter decile cutoffs are only known after the quarter ends; a close-above-high signal can only be acted on at the next session's open.
decision: Selection will use a threshold known ex ante (trailing distribution or fixed abnormal-return cutoff); all entries execute at the next open after the signal close. Recorded as a change from the proposal.

observation_or_problem: Pre-run environment check: disk had 2.4 GiB free; pandas/numpy not installed; network not yet verified for the brief's access rules.
action_or_experiment: Checked IP, disk, Python, git and GitHub CLI before any API work.
result: Disk nearly full, scientific stack missing.
decision: Created a uv-managed venv; candidate freed disk; API client built with a pre-flight guard (geo check configurable via REQUIRE_HK_IP), header-only key auth and no key in URLs or logs. Candidate uses his own purchased Massive subscription rather than the club key (disclosed in README).

observation_or_problem: Massive docs: 8-K Disclosures and SEC EDGAR Index endpoints expose filing_date only, no time of day; Ticker Events supports only ticker_change events.
action_or_experiment: Read the full Massive REST docs dump for every endpoint named in the proposal.
result: The proposal's plan to classify before-open vs after-close reports from Massive 8-K timestamps is infeasible; delistings must come from All Tickers active=false (delisted_utc), not Ticker Events.
decision: Announcement time will come from SEC EDGAR submissions JSON acceptanceDateTime (free, public, point-in-time) for 8-Ks whose items include 2.02; delistings from All Tickers. Change from proposal.

observation_or_problem: Disk budget rules out tick-level NBBO quotes for spread estimation.
action_or_experiment: Sized quote data against free disk.
decision: Transaction costs will use the Corwin-Schultz high-low spread estimator from daily bars plus a fixed commission assumption; reported gross and net. Change from proposal.

observation_or_problem: Probed the account with one call per endpoint (scripts/probe_access.py).
action_or_experiment: Daily Market Summary 2004/2010/2016/2026, tickers point-in-time, splits, dividends, income statements, quotes, Benzinga earnings, 8-K disclosures, EDGAR index.
result: Full price history from 2004 available; splits/dividends/income statements OK; Benzinga Earnings returned HTTP 403 (not entitled); 8-K Disclosures start 2020-01-02.
decision: Sample period can start in 2005 (Item 2.02 numbering began Aug 2004). Benzinga is unavailable, so EDGAR acceptance timestamps are the primary event source, not a fallback. EPS surprise, if used, must come from Income Statements.

observation_or_problem: Massive 8-K Disclosures taxonomy label for earnings is quarterly_earnings; on 2024-01-25 (peak season) only 9 of 205 classified filings carried it.
action_or_experiment: Pulled the 119-row taxonomy and category counts for a known heavy earnings day.
result: The endpoint badly undercounts earnings releases even after 2020 and cannot define the event sample.
decision: Do not use Massive 8-K Disclosures as the event source; EDGAR Item 2.02 is used throughout. Change from proposal.

observation_or_problem: Need point-in-time, survivorship-free prices with explicit adjustment.
action_or_experiment: Downloading Daily Market Summary with adjusted=false for every weekday 2004-2026 (about 5,900 calls, parquet per year), All Tickers (active and delisted, 36,588 rows), Splits (27,541 rows).
result: About 35 MB per year; SPY present on every day; 0 failed calls so far.
decision: Store unadjusted bars and apply split factors ourselves (product of split_from/split_to for later splits), so price filters use true historical price levels and the adjustment is testable.

observation_or_problem: EDGAR submissions at one request per 0.11 s achieved under 1 request/s because each response takes 0.4-2 s.
action_or_experiment: Restarted the EDGAR job with 8 threads behind a shared 9 req/s limiter (within the SEC's 10 req/s rule).
result: About 3.8 CIKs/s; 9,679 unique CIKs for 11,929 US common-stock tickers; roughly 70 Item 2.02 8-Ks per company.
decision: Proceed; record per-CIK coverage so the report can state how many tickers lack a CIK or filings.

observation_or_problem: Compared our cumulative split factors with the vendor's historical_adjustment_factor and our adjusted closes with vendor-adjusted per-ticker aggregates for nine split tickers.
action_or_experiment: Local factor comparison over 18,628 tickers; API cross-check on 2004-2008 closes.
result: Factors match for all but 132 tickers, all of which are same-day double splits where only row order differs; adjusted closes match on split days, but 0.2-1% of days show >1% differences between the two vendor endpoints (unrelated to splits).
decision: Keep our adjustment; use the grouped endpoint consistently for all returns; add tests/test_prices.py and tests/test_api_crosscheck.py; note the endpoint discrepancy as a data-quality limitation.

observation_or_problem: Six-lens review of the proposal (methodology, data feasibility, brief compliance, execution, interviewer, literature) found that Rule A exceeds Rule B by construction on every breakout event, because A's return equals the pre-breakout run-up times B's post-breakout leg.
action_or_experiment: Re-derived the identity A = (P_k/P_1) x (P_T/P_k), B = P_T/P_k with P_k > high_0 >= P_1.
result: B > A can only arise from non-breakout events doing badly; the proposal's headline test measures a momentum filter, not the timing of drift.
decision: Primary test changed to a within-event decomposition (per-day abnormal return before vs after breakout) with fixed-delay and unanchored-level controls and a matched non-earnings placebo; B vs A retained as a secondary result. Recorded as change from proposal; see docs/PLAN.md.

observation_or_problem: EDGAR acceptance times classify 145,809 filtered filings as before-open or after-close and 36,118 as intraday (09:30-16:00 ET). The absolute abnormal return peaks on the assigned day 0 for 64% of bmo/amc events and on day +1 for 20-23%; for intraday filings it peaks on day +1 in 48% of cases.
result: Some 8-Ks are accepted after the press release, so a minority of events are dated one session late; intraday filings are the most ambiguous.
decision: Keep EDGAR dating (only point-in-time source available); exclude intraday filings from the main sample and report them as a robustness variant; state the misdating share as a limitation. Did NOT re-date events to the peak-return day because that would use ex-post information.

observation_or_problem: Default cell W=10, H=40 on 14,770 events: Rule A CAR +0.55% (2005-2014 +1.43%, 2015-2026 +0.12%); Rule B +0.21%; B minus A -0.34% overall and -0.92% [CI -1.41, -0.46] in 2005-2014. Breakout events: A +4.19%, B +0.34%; non-breakout events A -5.10%. Post-breakout per-day AR +0.01%/day.
action_or_experiment: scripts/run_main.py with decomposition, controls C and D1-D3, calendar-time Newey-West tests.
result: The 'post minus pre per-day' statistic first planned is dominated by the mechanically conditioned pre-breakout leg (+2.28%/day) and is uninformative about timing.
decision: Primary statistic redefined BEFORE looking at the grid: post-breakout per-day AR minus the season- and event-day-matched unconditional path (analysis.py::matched_control). The pre/post split is kept as a descriptive table with the conditioning stated.

action_or_experiment: scripts/run_grid.py; selection criterion = largest lower CI bound of the primary statistic in 2005-2014.
result: Primary statistic within +/-3 bp/day of zero in every cell and period; B minus A negative in all 12 selection cells (CI below zero in 11), CI includes zero in all 12 hold-out cells. Chosen cell W=15, H=40; hold-out primary -1.6 bp/day [-5.2, +2.0].
decision: Report the default and the chosen cell plus the full grid; conclusion is parameter-invariant, so no further tuning.

observation_or_problem: Variants: day-2 trigger, market-on-close fills, fixed 5% and z0>=2 selection, intraday included, no-news placebo 60 sessions earlier, short-side mirror, Friday split, liquidity and range terciles; Corwin-Schultz spreads (median 0.82%).
action_or_experiment: scripts/run_robustness.py; every variant logged in logs/experiment_record.csv.
result: All variants agree; the placebo reproduces B < A without any news, confirming the pattern is mechanical; net of half-spread + 5 bp per side Rule A is -0.52% and Rule B -0.45%. Friday events show negative post-breakout drift (-4.0 bp/day, CI excludes zero) but it is one of many splits.
decision: Conclusion: hypothesis rejected; drift after extreme reactions exists only before 2015 and is not tradable net. Friday result reported as a curiosity, not a finding. Matched non-earnings placebo left as future work (time).

observation_or_problem: Brief requires the report to map to its list of contents and to the enumerated acceptable conclusions.
action_or_experiment: Wrote docs/report.md, README parameter table and disclosure, exported PDF.
result: Conclusion maps to 'original result caused by a methodological issue' (the timing test) and 'exists before costs but not tradable' (the early-sample drift).
decision: Submit with negative result; no further experiments to avoid searching for a positive.

observation_or_problem: The first report draft was accurate but dense; the candidate needs to understand and defend every sentence, and graders value clear reasoning over length.
action_or_experiment: Rewrote the report in plain language with a toy example of the A/B identity, a glossary, likely interview questions, and one source of text (scripts/report_content.py) that generates both notebooks/report.ipynb (executed, code shown) and docs/report.md; exported aggregate-only tables so the notebook runs from the public repo without licensed data.
result: Notebook executes with no errors from outputs/ alone; report and notebook cannot diverge.
decision: Submit the notebook as the interactive report and the markdown/PDF as the concise written report; numbers unchanged.

observation_or_problem: The brief asks for important assumptions to be logged explicitly.
action_or_experiment: Listed the choices fixed a priori in docs/PLAN.md at 02:05 before any result: $5 minimum price, $1M median 60-day dollar volume, 120 prior bars, trailing-four-quarter 90th percentile cut, 20-session de-duplication, SPY as benchmark, Corwin-Schultz window days -25..-6, 5 bp commission per side, default cell W=10 H=40.
result: None of these was tuned; sensitivity to the cut-off (85th/95th percentile) and to stricter price ($10) and liquidity ($5M) filters was added as robustness rows R13-R16 and changes nothing.
decision: Keep the a-priori values; report the sensitivity table instead of optimising.

observation_or_problem: A second review of the finished submission found that the matched control for the primary statistic used close-to-close daily returns (so it included the overnight gap into the entry day, which the position never receives) and that its season lookup was by row position, which misaligned filtered subsets.
action_or_experiment: Rewrote analysis.matched_control to use the identical open(e)->close(H) span for both sides and to align seasons by index; re-ran grid, robustness (adding R13-R16 sensitivities and cost rows by period) and aggregates.
result: Primary statistic moved from -0.7 bp/day [-3.0, +1.6] to -0.9 [-1.5, -0.2]; the interval tightened and now excludes zero on the negative side. Grid-selected cell changed from W=15,H=40 to W=20,H=60. Rule A and B numbers unchanged.
decision: Report the corrected numbers; conclusion unchanged and slightly stronger (post-breakout drift is, if anything, below the normal path, consistent with short-term reversal). Both the error and the correction are recorded here.

observation_or_problem: The proposal listed dividends as an adjustment input; the analysis uses split-adjusted price returns only.
result: Over 40-session windows dividends change returns by a few basis points and cancel in the same-day matched comparison.
decision: Do not add dividend adjustment; state as a limitation and as change #8 from the proposal.
